Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the standard setuptools.build_meta backend and defines only a normal console_scripts entry point: vinod = vinod.cli:cli.
  • No evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, install-time setup.py execution, custom PEP 517 build hooks, or malicious import-time side effects was found.
  • vinod init can register a Claude Code MCP server and Stop hook (vinod session-end), but this requires the user to run the CLI and is documented application behavior, not install-time automatic execution.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • **Credential harvesting:** No evidence of broad discovery of environment variables, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI/CD tokens, wallet files, or similar secrets.

- The code reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and an api_key from ~/.vinod/config.json, which appears to be a single documented credential for Claude session summarization and is not paired with broad harvesting behavior.

  • **Exfiltration/networking:** The package may call the Claude API through the anthropic SDK for session summarization when an API key is configured. This appears to be normal functionality, with no evidence of suspicious C2, webhooks, raw IP endpoints, or paste/drop-service uploads.
  • **Staging:** No evidence of tar/zip/gzip/base64 archive staging or hidden temporary collection of harvested files.
  • **Persistence:** No evidence of systemd units, cron jobs, launch agents, shell profile edits, background polling loops, or self-reinstall logic. Claude Code Stop hook registration appears to be user-triggered application configuration via vinod init.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence of Kubernetes, Docker socket, cloud metadata, GitHub Actions/CI tokens, or package registry token usage.
  • **Obfuscation/loaders:** No evidence of base64/zlib/marshal/eval/exec/compile loaders, encrypted payloads, downloader stubs, or self-deleting droppers. The pre-scan “encrypted-payload-primitive” match in README/PKG-INFO appears to be a false positive from ordinary prose.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The artifact contains expected package files under src/vinod, standard egg-info, README, pyproject.toml, and setup.cfg; no hidden payloads or unexplained native binaries were observed.
  • Dependencies are limited to click>=8.1.0 and anthropic>=0.40.0, consistent with the described CLI and Claude integration.
  • src/vinod/__init__.py has __version__ = "0.1.0" while package metadata says 0.3.2; this is a version mismatch but not, by itself, evidence of a malicious supply-chain attack.
  • Wheel/sdist mismatch cannot be assessed from the provided sdist extraction alone.
